subject: Post-call: capacity handshake and staged commit for Aegis Therapeutics
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Laura Stein <laura.stein@aegisthera.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: capacity handshake and staged commit for Aegis Therapeutics

Hi Laura — thanks again for a productive call this morning. Quick recap while it's fresh and a proposed next steps list so we don't lose momentum.

Summary of pain & goals
- Primary pain: unpredictable inference cost and occasional latency spikes at peak (clinical inference during report generation).
- Goal: deterministic throughput for nightly batch runs + sub-500ms p95 for interactive clinician queries.
- Compliance: data isolation and audit logs for PHI required; on-prem or VPC private deployment options on the table.

Redwood proposal (high level)
- Reserved capacity (Dedicated) proposal: initial committed pool of 8x A100-80GB equivalent GPUs (quantized model path supported).
- Isolation: tenant-isolated pool with private VPC peering + KMS key integration for encryption-in-use/logging.
- Scaling model: staged burst policy — baseline reserved pool (8 GPUs) with burst to shared capacity up to +4 GPUs during overnight batch windows.
- SLA targets: 99.9% monthly uptime; latency SLO targets we discussed: p50 ~120ms, p95 <= 500ms for the clinician flows (depends on sequence length / model).

Risks & assumptions
- Model size & perf: assumption is a 30–40B model family using 4-bit quantization for production; we may need an extra GPU in the pool if KV-cache hit rates are low.
- Procurement window: procurement and security review expected to be a 4–6 week path based on your timeline.

Next actions (owner / ETA)
1) I attach a rough capacity estimate (MVP) — Ben to confirm micro-benchmark assumptions and revise numbers — owner: Ben (EOD Thu 11 Jun).
2) Laura / Mark: share the security questionnaire & SOC2 contact or upload to the Doc Share — owner: Aegis (by end of next week 13 Jun).
3) Redwood to produce a 1-page Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and a staged commercial outline (trial -> commit) — owner: Mateo (draft by Wed 09 Jun).
4) Schedule a 60-min technical runbook sync with your infra team (we propose Wed 16 Jun) — owner: Grace to coordinate.

Attachments: aegis-mvp-capacity-estimate.xlsx (spreadsheet), MAP-draft-aegis-v1.pdf (draft)

If any of the above doesn't match what you heard, call it out and I'll update. Otherwise I'll push the MAP draft and Ben will follow up on the perf assumptions.

Thanks,
Mateo Alvarez

Thanks Mateo — that matches our notes. A few clarifications from our side:
- The 500ms p95 target is for the clinician UI only; some of our internal batch transformations can tolerate higher latency.
- Procurement: we need the SOC2 artifact and a completed security questionnaire to move to legal. I've uploaded a stub of our questionnaire here: https://aegis.fileshare/q1 (we'll finish the vendor upload by Tue).
- Timeline: if we can get a MAP and a short trial agreement this week, procurement will prioritize it — likely a 30-day technical trial followed by a commit conversation.

I'll coordinate the ops+infra invite for Wed 16 Jun if that still works.

Quick tech notes (following Mateo's draft):
- The MVP estimate assumes the 30B family quantized to 4-bit using our q4f16 path; we should run a short perf sweep (latency + memory footprint) to validate that 8x A100-80GB-equivalent hits the p95 target with typical batch sizes.
- If the batch windows are very bursty (e.g., >2x baseline throughput for >30m), recommend a burst-to-shared with autoscale cap rather than permanently adding GPUs to the reserved pool. That reduces unit cost.
- Ops ask: we'll need SSH jumpbox access + a 1-hour benchmark window where Aegis can run a representative workload; suggested window: Mon 14 Jun 02:00-03:00 UTC.

I'll take the attached spreadsheet and add a perf sensitivity tab by EOD Thu (11 Jun).

—Ben
